newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt court rejects Copt convert divorce case.
newsitem.headline: Egypt court rejects Copt convert divorce case.

text.p: An Egyptian court denied a man a divorce on Wednesday even after he converted from Coptic Christianity to Islam, a religion that gives men the right to automatic divorce, court officials said.
Judge Emad Khaled at the Cairo Civil Status court said that by changing his religion while the case was still pending, the unnamed husband had tried to circumvent the law.
Like the Roman Catholic Church, the Coptic church allows couples to divorce only in very rare cases. The rules for divorce in Islam, the dominant religion in Egypt, are much less strict.
The sources said the man had told the court he wanted to divorce his wife because she was not doing her "marital duties".

He then went to al-Azhar, Sunni Islam's most respected seat of learning, and obtained a certificate that he had converted to Islam. The judge rejected his divorce request after hearing the testimony of the Christian wife and her witnesses.
Egyptian courts apply Islamic marriage and divorce law on Moslem couples and church law on Christian couples.
